question: In the oil shale kerogen study, at what heating rate and with what sample mass was the experiment run whose evolved gases were analysed by FTIR and MS?
expect: the STA-FTIR-MS test on extracted kerogen: about 10 mg at 10 C/min to 800 C (sec. 2.3.4)
trap: the TGA's 5 mg at 5, 10 and 15 C/min
rendered:
<document title="A Study on Pyrolysis Characteristics and Product Release Mechanisms of Oil Shale">

=== page 2 ===
- 2.3.4. STA-FTIR-MS Coupled Testing. Online monitoring of product evolution was performed using a simultaneous thermal analyzer (NETZSCH STA 449 F3) coupled with a Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Nicolet iS50) and a mass spectrometer (NETZSCH QMS403D). Approximately 10 mg of extracted kerogen was heated from room temperature to 800 °C at 10 °C min^−1 under air or nitrogen.

The answer is: 10 mg of extracted kerogen was heated from room temperature to 800 °C at 10 °C min^−1 under air or nitrogen.
